A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterLCM research. All 33 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original face-restoration experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets in Table 1, alongside ablations, robustness analyses, and additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative and qualitative face-restoration experiments, ablations, and appendix analyses reported in v1.

M1.justification: The second-step LCM initialization, Visual Module, Spatial Encoder, sampling procedure, and training losses are unchanged. Section 3.2 adds only a reference to an existing Figure 8 example.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FFHQ training and CelebA-Test, LFW-Test, WebPhoto-Test, and WIDER-Test evaluation. Appendix scenarios involving tattoos, face paint, varying degradation, and natural images are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and the appendix comparisons. The same backbone variants and super-resolution comparators remain evaluated in Tables 6–9 and Figure 18.

E3.justification: The dataset sizes, degradation process, image resolution, evaluation metrics, training settings, and inference procedures remain identical. No new evaluation protocol is introduced in the main text or appendices.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices C–E retain the same encoder, starting-step, loss, backbone, noise-robustness, and input-condition analyses. The new Figure 8 reference points to an existing ablation without adding evidence.

E5.justification: The random-noise examples in Appendix C.2 and seed-variation statement in Appendix F are unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–10 and qualitative result figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports InterLCM CelebA-Test LPIPS of 0.223, FID of 45.38, and inference time of 0.421 seconds in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the mathematical descriptions of diffusion and consistency sampling, and Appendix E.6's derivation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic consistency, few-step restoration, perceptual-loss integration, restoration quality, and inference speed.

C2.justification: The explanation that visual embeddings alone cannot preserve global structure is unchanged; v2 merely points to Figure 8. Limitations concerning hands, intricate tattoos, severe degradation, and complex natural-image textures are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same initialization, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training iterations, hardware, and data-processing details. Project and baseline access links, including their hyperlink targets, are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to diffusion, consistency, and restoration methods are unchanged. Text crossing different page boundaries does not add or remove citations.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Nankai affiliation for three authors, corrects punctuation in the SoftBank affiliation, and adds a pointer to example 1 in Figure 8 within Section 3.2. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added affiliation produces local text reflow across pages 1–4, and the Figure 8 reference reflows the Spatial Encoder paragraph. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added affiliation and reference to the existing Figure 8 ablation provide small metadata and navigation refinements. The method, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality effectively the same.
